hints: Think about the colour of aqueous bromine to start with, and what happens to that colour when bromine is used up in a reaction.
Remember that bromination of phenylamine gives a substituted organic solid that is insoluble in water, so what type of observation would that produce?
walkthrough:
Picture the bromine water first**
You know aqueous bromine is a familiar orange to brown solution. Whenever bromine reacts and is consumed, that colour disappears. So one thing to look for here is decolourisation to colourless, which tells you a reaction has happened.

Think about the organic product**
Phenylamine is very reactive toward electrophilic substitution because the $\text{NH}_2$ group strongly activates the benzene ring. With bromine water it forms a tribromo substituted product which is a solid and insoluble in water. An insoluble solid appearing in a solution is seen as a white precipitate.

Final answer: Aqueous bromine is decolourised from orange / brown to colourless.
A white precipitate is formed.

hints: Compare the structures: ethylamine, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$, has no benzene ring, so can it undergo bromination of a ring like phenylamine does?
walkthrough:
Spot why ethylamine is different**
The reaction in (a) is substitution into an activated benzene ring. Ethylamine, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$, is an aliphatic amine with no aromatic ring to brominate. There is no equivalent electrophilic substitution available, so aqueous bromine is not consumed and you see no change.
Final answer: No change / no reaction. Bromine remains orange / brown and no precipitate forms.

hints: Recall that the $\text{NH}_2$ group is strongly 2,4 directing, and with excess bromine all available 2,4,6 positions on the phenylamine ring react.
walkthrough:
Use the activating power of NH2**
The lone pair on nitrogen in $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$ is donated into the benzene ring, making it so reactive that bromination occurs instantly in water with no catalyst needed. The $\text{NH}_2$ group directs incoming electrophiles to the 2, 4 and 6 positions (the two ortho positions and the para position).

Draw the excess product**
With excess aqueous bromine, all three of those positions are substituted. Keep the $\text{NH}_2$ group at the top of the ring (position 1) and place a Br atom at each side ortho position and one directly opposite at the para position. That gives a symmetrical tribromo product with formula $\text{C}_6\text{H}_2\text{Br}_3\text{NH}_2$.
Final answer: 2,4,6-tribromophenylamine: benzene ring with $\text{NH}_2$ at position 1 and Br atoms at positions 2, 4 and 6.

hints: Name the structure by counting the three bromo substituents relative to the amine group at position 1, using numbers to show their locations.
walkthrough:
Name from the ring you drew**
The parent is aniline, which is the same as phenylamine, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$. You have added three identical Br substituents at the two ortho positions and the para position relative to $\text{NH}_2$. Numbering from $\text{NH}_2$ as position 1, that is 2,4,6-tribromoaniline, also accepted as 2,4,6-tribromophenylamine.
